summary: Both sides draw the same full-saturation rainbow spanning the rig exactly once, but the port scrolls it ~4.8x too fast at the harness default and frays it with independent per-pixel hue noise the original never shows — the original's whole-strip offset stays perfectly uniform (residual RMS 0.0004 = quantization) out to 620 s.
observations: STRUCTURE (matches exactly): both sides render hue = pixelIndex/pixelCount + phase(t) at saturation 1.000 and value 1.000 on every pixel of every frame; both span exactly one hue cycle across the rig regardless of pixel count (span 0.917 cyc at --pixels 12, 0.997 cyc at --pixels 300, i.e. slope exactly 1/N per pixel on both), so both are index-driven and resolution-independent in the same way. On --rig grid --grid 16x16 both become the same horizontal rainbow banding.

RANDOMNESS — THE HEADLINE DIFFERENCE. Original: zero. Fitting each dumped frame's unwrapped hue profile to a line, the original's residual RMS is 0.0004 cycles at t=0, 10, 30, 60, 120, 180, 239 and still 0.0005 at t=600/610/619.8 — that is the 8-bit quantization floor, not noise. Every pixel carries the identical hue offset, i.e. the offset is perfectly 'synchronized' across the strip. Port: each pixel carries its OWN offset that wanders. Port residual RMS grows 0.0027 (t=0) -> 0.0212 (t=10) -> 0.0392 (t=30) -> 0.0491 (t=60) -> 0.0682 (t=120) -> 0.0827 (t=239) and plateaus near 0.089 (max deviation +/-0.25 cycles) by t=600. Neighbour-to-neighbour hue step SD reaches 0.131 cycles against an intended step of 0.0167 — ~8x the design step — so by a minute in the ramp is visibly zig-zagged and streaky.

The port's per-pixel noise is PERSISTENT, not per-frame sparkle: frame-to-frame residual change SD is 0.0029 while the standing residual is 10-30x larger, and the waterfall shows vertical streaks (a pixel holds its offset for many frames and drifts). Baseline motion stat 6.5 (port) vs 1.1 (orig) at 20 fps; survey 26 vs 13 at 5 fps; late window 26 vs 13.

MOTION SPEED: at the harness default 20 fps the original advances 0.002636 +/- 0.000082 cycles per frame = 0.0527 cyc/s (a full colour cycle every ~19 s); the port advances 0.012694 cycles per frame = 0.2539 cyc/s (full cycle every ~3.9 s). Port is 4.8x too fast at the default rate. Both scroll in the same direction at <=30 fps.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING DIVERGES. The original is a hybrid: measured per-frame hue step fits step = 0.1525*dt - 0.00496 cycles almost exactly (predicted vs observed: dt=0.2 -> 0.02554/0.02554, dt=0.1 -> 0.01029/0.01029, dt=0.05 -> 0.00267/0.00264, dt=0.025 -> -0.00115/-0.00118). So the original's scroll rate is 0.128 / 0.103 / 0.053 / 0.003 / -0.007 / -0.047 / -0.147 cyc/s at 5 / 10 / 20 / 30 / 32 / 40 / 60 fps — it slows with rising fps, stalls near 30.5 fps and RUNS BACKWARDS above it. The port is purely time-based: 0.2530 / 0.2531 / 0.2539 / 0.2548 / 0.2554 / 0.2545 / 0.2547 cyc/s at those same seven rates, forward always.

The constant -0.00496 cyc/frame term in the original is the whole of its fps dependence and has zero variance (per-frame step SD 0.000082 over 30 consecutive frames at 20 fps = quantization). RE-JUDGE NOTE: for a pattern named 'Synchronized Random Numbers' that term is exactly where a once-per-frame, shared-by-all-pixels random draw would sit, and it is rendering as a fixed constant. So on this engine the ORIGINAL still shows no randomness at all after the 2026-08-23 random(negative max) fix. I confirmed the engine binary is current (cargo build --bin luxel at HEAD 782acba, then re-rendered: dumps byte-identical to the pre-rebuild run) and provenance is stable (portSha256 4b26d61b2b96, epeSha256 5950edcf94f4, harnessSha256 40eb475a94b8). Whether that constant is a genuine constant in the pattern or a still-degenerate random() is not decidable from output.

DETERMINISM: neither side responds to --seed (1, 7, 1234, 99999 all produce byte-identical frames on both sides) nor to --wall-clock (1756000000, 1756043210, 1600000000 all byte-identical on both sides). Seed/clock independence is shared behaviour and is plausibly the point of the pattern; it is not a divergence.

SINGLE REGIME, NO MODES: a 60 s / 5 fps survey and a 240 s / 2-5 fps extension show one uninterrupted regime on both sides — a diagonal rainbow waterfall with no boundaries, flashes, resets or palette walks. The original's stats are constant to the digit over the whole 240 s (meanBrightness/meanR/meanG/meanB all min=max=127, motion pinned at 13 at 5 fps, zeroMotionFrames 0). The port's channel means wander in 109..146 from its noise but brightnessTrend is 'steady' on both.

STEADY STATE: at --skip 600 --seconds 20 the original is still the identical clean rainbow (circular residual RMS 0.0004-0.0005) and the port is still the frayed one (0.088-0.090, max dev 0.25). Neither side dies, saturates, freezes or decays; the divergence is fully established by ~60 s and stable thereafter.
CONTROL SURFACE: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' on BOTH sides. Matching (empty) control surfaces — no dial to test and no missing/extra dial to report.
feedback: Slow the hue scroll. At the harness default 20 fps the original advances 0.00264 cycles/frame (0.0527 cyc/s, ~19 s per full rainbow); the port advances 0.01269 cycles/frame (0.254 cyc/s, ~3.9 s). Divide the port's rate by ~4.8 to match at 20 fps. Caveat for the fixer: the original's rate is fps-dependent (step = 0.1525*dt - 0.00496 cyc), so if the -0.00496 per-frame term turns out to be a degenerate random that should average out, the correct time-based target is ~0.1525 cyc/s and the port is then only ~1.67x too fast. Match at 20 fps first, then re-check at 5/40 fps.

Make the random contribution SYNCHRONIZED — one draw per frame applied identically to every pixel — instead of per-pixel. The original's rendered strip has literally zero pixel-to-pixel deviation from a clean ramp (residual RMS 0.0004 cycles = quantization) at every time from t=0 to t=620 s; the port reaches 0.089 RMS with +/-0.25-cycle excursions and neighbour steps ~8x the intended 1/N. That per-pixel fray is the single most visible difference and it defeats the pattern's namesake property.

Stop the port's per-pixel offset from ACCUMULATING. It is a slow random walk, not per-frame sparkle: it starts small (RMS 0.0027 at t=0), builds over the first ~60 s and only plateaus near 0.089 by ~t=600 s. So the port looks nearly right for the first second or two and progressively degrades — a fix that only checks a 6 s baseline will miss it. Any per-pixel randomness must be re-derived each frame (or dropped entirely), never integrated into a persistent per-pixel phase.

Frame-rate coupling: the port's scroll is purely time-based (0.253-0.255 cyc/s identical at 5/10/20/30/32/40/60 fps) while the original's has a fixed per-frame component that makes it slow with rising fps and reverse direction above ~30.5 fps. If the per-frame term is meant to be a random draw, a correct port should reproduce a once-per-frame draw (which is inherently frame-coupled), not a smooth per-second advance.

Everything else already matches and should not be touched: the spatial law (exactly one hue cycle across the rig, index-driven, resolution-independent from 12 to 300 px and on a 16x16 grid), full saturation and full value on every pixel, seed independence and wall-clock independence, single-regime behaviour with no modes, and the empty control surface.
